title: Casper and the Landfall
premise: August Okonkwo, a desert ranger who has spent seven years outrunning a betrayal she committed as a young soldier, is the only soul who notices when a government survey team vanishes from the salt flats without tracks. Following their abandoned gear, she finds them alive but altered—carrying a discovery beneath the landfall that the state will kill to bury. August must lead the survivors home through the coming monsoon while deciding whether her own buried truth is the price the expedition demands. In the end she delivers them to safety, confesses her past, and chooses loyalty to the living over loyalty to the lie she built her life on.
about_author: Juniper Montrose is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote basins before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who would rather walk away than be known.

chapters.title: Salt and Static
chapters.summary: August's POV. On a routine patrol across the flats, August intercepts signs of a thief she's tracked for months—then finds them dead, and beyond them, a government survey camp abandoned mid-meal. Radios hiss static; the desert is too quiet. The beat is unease: her instinct to keep moving wars with the first pull to stop and look closer.

chapters.title: The Team That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a flashback to her army years. She catalogs the camp: gear intact, no tracks leaving, a journal page torn out. Flashbacks reveal the betrayal she fled—she once erased a patrol from the record to save herself. The beat is dread layered with guilt; the missing team mirrors the people she erased.

chapters.title: Tracks Against the Wind
chapters.summary: August's POV. A dust storm erases the flats, and in its wake she finally finds footprints—eleven sets, walking in perfect unison toward the old mining shafts. She follows against every survival instinct. The beat is compulsion: for the first time in years, August chooses pursuit over escape.

chapters.title: What the Shaft Kept
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Imani Reyes, the survey team's young geologist, writing a hidden log. Deep in the shafts, the team found a pre-monsoon civilization's records—proof the government's landfall maps are deliberate lies. Their leader, Dr. Halloran, has ordered silence. The beat is claustrophobia and the first fracture inside the team.

chapters.title: Eleven Walking
chapters.summary: August's POV. She catches the team on the surface at night and finds them hollow-eyed, marching under Halloran's command, refusing rescue. Imani slips her the stolen journal pages. The beat is confrontation: August recognizes in Halloran the same machinery of enforced silence she once served.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Ledger
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Halloran reveals the state knew about the shafts all along; the survey was a containment exercise, and the team's 'rescue' was never planned. Imani secretly signals August with a mirror flash. The beat is betrayal crystallizing into resolve—the team begins choosing each other over the mission.

chapters.title: Water on the Horizon
chapters.summary: August's POV. The monsoon front appears on the horizon, days early. August proposes a brutal route through the canyon country that might outrun the flood, but it means trusting her with their lives. Halloran counters with an offer: her old record scrubbed clean if she walks away. The beat is temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Long Crossing
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating through Imani, team medic Osei, and August. The crossing through the canyons turns desperate as flash floods chase them; August's desert craft saves them twice, and Halloran's authority finally breaks when he abandons a straggler and August goes back. The beat is found family forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the canyon mouth, the monsoon hits in full force. Halloran, cornered, tries to destroy the records; August stops him, and in the struggle the truth of her own erased patrol spills out to Imani and the team. The beat is the climax: loyalty and truth collide, and August stops running.

chapters.title: What We Carry Out
chapters.summary: August's POV, weeks later. The team reaches the ranger station; August files a report containing everything—the shafts, the lies, her own confession—knowing it may cost her everything. Imani and the others stand with her. The beat is resolution: August has stopped moving away, and for the first time, staying costs exactly what it should.
